english.title: Non-consensual analysis of DNA - Human Tissue Act 2004
english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) had in your possession bodily material, namely **(..SPECIFY THE MATERIAL..), intending that human DNA in the material be analysed without qualifying consent and the results of that analysis be used otherwise than for an excepted purpose as provided by Part 2 of Schedule 4 to the Human Tissue Act 2004
english.legislation: Contrary to section 45 of the Human Tissue Act 2004.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i)Section 45(1) of the Human Tissue Act 2004 provides exceptions to the offence where the material is of a kind excepted under section 45(2) of the Act and where the person does reasonably believe the material to be of a kind so excepted.
(ii) Schedule 4 of the Act makes provision for the interpretation of qualifying consentand use for an excepted purpose.
(iii)Section 45(5) of the Act provides that bodily material means material which has come from a human body, and consists of or includes human cells.

other.penalty:
Summary: A fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
Indictment: Three years imprisonment and/or a fine.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
